subject: Post-call: SDK auth & model-routing options for Ava Systems integration
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ava Systems <eng+integration@avasystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: SDK auth & model-routing options for Ava Systems integration

Hi Tim / Ava team,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — good call. Quick recap + proposed next steps based on the architecture discussion:  

What we covered (short):
- Integration surface: you plan to integrate Redwood inference via our SDK for embedding lookups and text generation, plus a reranker for search relevance.
- Auth: will need token-based service account for server-side calls (no client-secret in browsers), and optional mTLS for private deployments.
- Routing & policies: you want low-latency on US-EAST for interactive chat, cheaper batch embeddings routed to a lower-cost region, and automatic fallback to quantized model variants if top-tier capacity is saturated.
- Structured output / tool-calling: intent to use function/tool calls to trigger product DB lookups; will need schema enforcement in model responses.

Open technical questions we identified:
1) Do you want the SDK to make calls directly from your backend to Redwood, or route via your gateway for audit/KMS reasons?
2) Expected QPS for chat vs embedding/rerank workloads (rough split would help config defaults).
3) Will you require RPO/RTO guarantees (SLA) or is best-effort OK for initial rollout?

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- Rishi + Marissa: provide a small SDK example (server-side auth) and a sample routing-policy YAML for your team to review (attached).
- Ava: share target QPS and any compliance needs (e.g., must not leave VPC, KMS requirement).
- Schedule a 30-min architecture follow-up with your infra lead to confirm network path & mTLS details.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-example.patch (tiny server SDK snippet), routing-policy-proposal.yaml (initial policy draft), security-checklist.pdf

If this matches your notes, we can lock these actions and schedule the follow-up for next week.

Cheers,

Subject: Re: Post-call: SDK auth & model-routing options for Ava Systems integration

Rishi — thanks, that recap is spot on. A few answers and clarifications from our side:  

Answers:
- We'll call Redwood from our backend (service layer) behind our gateway; we need request-level auditing and want to keep keys in our KMS.
- Expected steady-state QPS: chat peak ~120 qps (US-EAST), embeddings batch jobs ~400 reqs/hour (can be queued), reranker calls ~50 qps during search peak.
- Compliance: must support customer-managed KMS and enterprise audit logs; SLA not mandatory for initial pilot but preferred.

Clarifying questions:
1) For the fallback chain: if primary model hits capacity, can we define an ordered list of model variants with explicit latency/cost thresholds?
2) For structured tool-calling: we need strong output validation — can we pin model versions for canary + automatic rollback on schema regression?

We'll share an internal diagram of where calls will originate from (gateway IP ranges, VPC peering notes) before the follow-up.

Tim

Head of Platform Integrations
Ava Systems

Subject: Re: Post-call: SDK auth & model-routing options for Ava Systems integration

Thanks Tim — great detail, that helps a lot. A couple of tactical notes and proposed answers to your clarifying questions:  

1) Fallback chains: yes — our routing-policy YAML allows ordered lists with conditional thresholds (e.g., if P99 latency > 350ms or queue length > 80, route to fallback-model-quant). We can also attach cost caps per-route so billing alerts trigger when a threshold is crossed. See routing-policy-proposal.yaml attachment (lines commented).

2) Version pinning & regressions: you can pin a route to a model version. We support canary rollouts (percentage split) and quality monitors tied to a prompt set; on regression we can trigger automatic rollback or a fail-open to a stable variant. We also support structured-output schemas and will reject responses that don't match (or flag them depending on policy).

Action items from Redwood:
- Rishi: send quick SDK server snippet (done, attached).
- Hiro: I'll loop Hiro to confirm network/TLS details and provide the expected IP ranges for VPC peering and optional mTLS cert exchange.
- Marissa: coordinate setting up a DH call next Tue with Ava infra (30 minutes).

We'll prepare a short demo showing routing policy behavior with a sample load to illustrate fallback in action. Would Tue 2026-03-23 at 10:00 PT work for your infra team?

—Marissa

Thanks — Tue 2026-03-23 10:00 PT works for us. Hiro, can you confirm you'll join to discuss VPC peering / mTLS details?

Tim, attaching a tiny example of a routing policy snippet here inline for quick reference:  

--- routing-policy-proposal.yaml (excerpt) ---
routes:
  - name: chat-low-latency
    preferred_region: us-east-1
    model_chain: [gptx-16b-fast, gptx-8b-quant]
    latency_policy:
      p50: 80ms
      p95: 220ms
      p99: 400ms
    failover_conditions:
      - metric: p99_latency
        operator: ">"
        value: "350ms"
      - metric: queue_length
        operator: ">"
        value: "80"
  - name: embeddings-batch
    preferred_region: us-central-1
    model_chain: [embed-6b-econ]
    batching: true
    cost_cap_per_1000: "$0.40"

--- end excerpt ---

I'll drop the full YAML and SDK snippet in Drive and share the link (in the Drive folder referenced above). Looking forward to the follow-up.

Rishi
